preconditions.description: The number of skewers n is an integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(p) == n and all(1 <= x <= n for x in p) and len(set(p)) == n
preconditions.description: The permutation p is a list of n integers where each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once.

preconditions.expression: len(b) == n and all(x in (0, 1) for x in b)
preconditions.description: The sequence b is a list of n integers, each being either 0 or 1.

postconditions.description: The output is a single non-negative integer string.

The output integer equals the minimum total number of changes required in p and b such that the resulting system allows every skewer to visit every position in both directions. Here, min_changes(n, p, b) is defined as the minimum sum of changes to p (to make it a valid permutation) and changes to b such that the functional graph of the permutation decomposes into cycles where the parity of the sum of b-values in each cycle is odd, or if the permutation is not a single cycle, the changes ensure the system becomes a single cycle with odd parity sum, or more generally, the system satisfies the condition that the state space (position, direction) is fully reachable from any starting state. Specifically, for a permutation decomposed into disjoint cycles, the condition for full reachability of all 2n states is that the permutation consists of a single cycle and the sum of b-values along that cycle is odd. If the permutation has multiple cycles, changes are needed to merge them into a single cycle, and the parity of the resulting cycle's b-sum must be odd. The cost is the number of elements changed in p plus the number of elements changed in b.
